stem.en: Archaeologists dig a site with no writing. They find a rich grave with gold beads, a hearth with charred grain, and the base of a wall. Which statement goes beyond what these objects can show?

text.en: The people here cooked or burned grain on a fire.

feedback.en: A hearth with charred grain is direct evidence of this, so the statement stays close to the objects.

text.en: Gold beads were placed in this grave.

feedback.en: The beads were found in the grave, so this is what the ground shows.

text.en: The person in the grave was the ruler of this village.
Someone here built a wall on this spot.

feedback.en: The base of the wall is there in the trench, so this stays close to the evidence.

explanation.en: A rich grave shows that someone was buried with valuable things. It cannot show a title or a job, because nobody's name or rank is written in the soil. The person could have been a ruler, but objects alone cannot tell us that.

hints.en: Which statement needs a name or a title that nobody wrote down?
